methods: We pooled odds ratios (OR) using a fixed-effect (Peto) model and the Wald z statistic. Studies were added in publication-year order. The required information size was 5,671 participants using a two-sided test with α = 0.05 and 80% power. The anticipated intervention effect was a Peto OR of 0.6738, the 95% CI limit closest to the null (Wetterslev 2017). The control event proportion was 4.49% (unweighted mean of control arms). The fixed-effect model does not adjust the information size for heterogeneity; a random-effects model gave D² = 94.8% and a required information size of 109,848 participants (Wetterslev 2017). Monitoring boundaries used Lan-DeMets O’Brien-Fleming spending. Futility boundaries were non-binding. Sensitivity analyses repeated the analysis with alternative anticipated intervention effects. The analysis used metafor 5.2-1 and gsDesign 3.11.0.

Comparison:  / Control

Methods
We pooled odds ratios (OR) using a random-effects model with the REML estimator of between-study variance and the Wald z statistic. Studies were added in table order. The required information size was 117,364 participants using a two-sided test with α = 0.05 and 80% power. The anticipated intervention effect was an OR of 0.6835, the 95% CI limit closest to the null (Wetterslev 2017). The control event proportion was 4.49% (unweighted mean of control arms). The information size was adjusted for D² = 94.8%. Monitoring boundaries used Lan-DeMets O’Brien-Fleming spending. Futility boundaries were non-binding. The penalised Z-curve used the law of the iterated logarithm with λ = 2 (Hu 2007). Sensitivity analyses repeated the analysis with alternative anticipated intervention effects. The analysis used metafor 5.2-1 and gsDesign 3.11.0.
Results
The cumulative Z-curve crossed the monitoring boundary favouring  when Hart  Sutherland was added (27,787 participants, 24% of the required information size). Accrued information is 304% of the required information size. The conventional 95% CI was 0.3296 to 0.6835. A TSA-adjusted CI is not reported because the required information size was reached. The final penalised Z-score was −2.085. Because the cumulative Z-curve crossed the monitoring boundary, the result remains statistically significant after accounting for repeated significance testing.

Trial Sequential Analysis —  · Binary · Odds ratio
Comparison:  / Control

Methods
We pooled odds ratios (OR) using a random-effects model with the REML estimator of between-study variance and the Wald z statistic. Studies were added in table order. The required information size was 176,782 participants using a two-sided test with α = 0.05 and 90% power. The anticipated intervention effect was an OR of 0.7 (entered). The control event proportion was 4.49% (unweighted mean of control arms). The information size was adjusted for D² = 94.8%. Monitoring boundaries used Lan-DeMets O’Brien-Fleming spending. Futility boundaries were non-binding. The penalised Z-curve used the law of the iterated logarithm with λ = 2 (Hu 2007). Sensitivity analyses repeated the analysis with alternative anticipated intervention effects. The analysis used metafor 5.2-1 and gsDesign 3.11.0.
Results
The cumulative Z-curve crossed the monitoring boundary favouring  when Hart  Sutherland was added (27,787 participants, 16% of the required information size). Accrued information is 202% of the required information size. The conventional 95% CI was 0.3296 to 0.6835. A TSA-adjusted CI is not reported because the required information size was reached. The final penalised Z-score was −2.085. Because the cumulative Z-curve crossed the monitoring boundary, the result remains statistically significant after accounting for repeated significance testing.
